newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan public fund buys dlrs and US notes - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Japan public fund buys dlrs and US notes - dealers.

text.p: A major Japanese public fund actively bought substantial amounts of U.S. government notes and dollars recently, dealers said on Thursday.
The public fund body had to convert yen into dollars on the foreign exchange market to buy the U.S. Treasuries.
"One major public fund is buying shorter-term U.S. Treasury notes almost everyday," said one bond dealer.
"The volume is also relatively heavy," he added.
In morning trade, some Japanese investors were detected buying 10-year notes, providing an overall firm tone to the U.S. Treasury market.
"It was unusual for ordinary investors to buy U.S. notes with the dollar at such a high level," said another bond dealer.
Some private investors such as life insurers were cashing in profits by liquidating parts of their holdings, although they were still net buyers of U.S. Treasuries, he added.

Currencies dealers also said that a Japanese public fund body continued to buy dollars even after the dollar rose above 120 yen. They added that this was one of driving forces behind the dollar pushing up against the yen recently.
The dollar briefly rose close to 124 yen in afternoon Tokyo on Thursday, despite an absence of fresh factors.
There was talk in the market on Thursday that the Postal Life Insurance Bureau (Kampo), one of the world's richest public funds, may have bought dollars, dealers said.
Kampo officials were not available to comment.
Its officials customarily decline to comment on Kampo investments on the grounds that to do so could invite speculation in the market. ---Tatsuo Ito, Tokyo treasury desk +81-3-3432-1396
